optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Model Evaluation Engineer, Wealth Services Platform
professionalSummary: Seasoned model evaluation specialist with a proven track record of maintaining evaluation harnesses, managing labelled review sets, and driving significant reductions in false-alert rates for wealth advisory platforms.
experienceHighlights: Maintained a Python-based evaluation harness scheduled on the platform’s batch runner, expanding the labelled adviser‑review set by 1,200 alerts over a year.
Executed pre‑release evaluations for four model versions, publishing comprehensive reports to model and operations teams.
Reduced adviser‑seen false‑alert rate from 31% (Q1) to 18% (Q4) through threshold recalibration in version 3.2, meeting documented quarterly baselines.
Coordinated release decisions in model release meetings, ensuring clear responsibility boundaries between model leads and adviser operations.
Authored evaluation notes detailing review‑set composition, known limitations (e.g., under‑representation of newly onboarded portfolios), and hand‑over items for subsequent evaluations.
projectsAndWorkSamples: Quarterly false‑alert report (rate per quarter, baseline line, version 3.2 marker) and evaluation notes for version 3.2, including batch runner job identifiers as verification trail.
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work samples establish the candidate’s experience with evaluation harness maintenance, labelled review set management, pre‑release evaluation execution, false‑alert rate reduction, release coordination, and documentation of evaluation assumptions and hand‑over conditions. They do not provide evidence of broader organizational impact beyond the wealth services platform or independent verification of the reported metrics.

decisionBoundary.statement: Candidate’s evidence supports all role requirements but further verification of metrics and stakeholder alignment is recommended.

role.roleTitle: Model Evaluation Engineer, Wealth Services Platform

evidence.text: Maintained the evaluation harness (Python, scheduled on the platform's batch runner) and the labelled review set of adviser-confirmed alerts, adding 1,200 newly labelled alerts over the year.
evidence.notes: Directly states maintenance of harness and labelled set.

evidence.text: Wrote the evaluation notes for each version, listing the review-set composition...
evidence.notes: Supports ongoing management of review set.

evidence.text: Ran the pre-release evaluation for each of the four model versions released in the year and published the evaluation report to the model team and adviser operations.
Work sample: the quarterly false-alert report (rate per quarter, baseline line, version 3.2 marker) and the evaluation notes for version 3.2...

The false-alert rate seen by advisers fell from 31 percent in Q1 to 18 percent in Q4 after the threshold recalibration I proposed was adopted in version 3.2, as measured on the labelled review set and reported against the documented Q1 baseline of 31 percent.

Reference call with former model team lead: confirmed the false-alert figures come from the quarterly evaluation report on the labelled set, that the threshold recalibration was the candidate's proposal, and the employment dates.
Coordinated release decisions in the model release meeting; the model team lead took the go/no-go decision and adviser operations confirmed the alert-volume impact.

Wrote the evaluation notes for each version, listing the review-set composition, the known limitation that alerts on newly onboarded portfolios were under-represented, and the hand-over items for the next evaluation.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate maintained the evaluation harness and expanded the labelled review set by 1,200 alerts.
supportedClaims.witness: Maintained the evaluation harness (Python, scheduled on the platform's batch runner) and the labelled review set of adviser-confirmed alerts, adding 1,200 newly labelled alerts over the year.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate ran pre-release evaluations for all four model versions and published reports.
supportedClaims.witness: Ran the pre-release evaluation for each of the four model versions released in the year and published the evaluation report to the model team and adviser operations.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate reduced the false-alert rate from 31% to 18% in Q4.
supportedClaims.witness: The false-alert rate seen by advisers fell from 31 percent in Q1 to 18 percent in Q4 after the threshold recalibration I proposed was adopted in version 3.2, as measured on the labelled review set and reported against the documented Q1 baseline of 31 percent.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate coordinated release decisions with model team and adviser operations.
supportedClaims.witness: Coordinated release decisions in the model release meeting; the model team lead took the go/no-go decision and adviser operations confirmed the alert-volume impact.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate documented evaluation assumptions, limitations, and hand-over items.
supportedClaims.witness: Wrote the evaluation notes for each version, listing the review-set composition, the known limitation that alerts on newly onboarded portfolios were under-represented, and the hand-over items for the next evaluation.

followUpQuestions.question: Can you describe the methodology used to calculate the false-alert rate and how you ensured its accuracy across different portfolio types?
followUpQuestions.evidenceTarget: Detailed explanation of calculation and validation process.

followUpQuestions.question: What specific documentation practices do you follow to capture evaluation assumptions and hand-over items?

humanReviewChecklist: Verify that the false-alert rate reduction is attributable to the candidate’s actions, not external changes.
Confirm that the evaluation harness is still operational and maintained post‑year.
Ensure that the candidate’s coordination role aligns with current release governance structures.
